The program plan can be found in document A/AT/6, Section 6, which was made available together with the CRP. Only Section A of document A/AT/6, Section 6, more specifically paragraphs 6.1, 6.24 is submitted for your consideration. The remaining parts of the document pertains to UNRWA's proposed program budget for the same period. As may be recalled, the annual session of the Committee often coincides with that of the General Assembly's Subsidiary Body for Planning, Program Coordination, the Committee for Programme and Coordination, CPC. Typically, despite the overlap, it was usually possible for the Committee to provide its inputs to the Programme Plan before the CPC concluded its work. This was not possible this year as the CPC concluded its session prior to the opening of COPUS, especially on Tuesday, 13 June. The CPC considered the Office's draft Programme Plan for 2016 on 15 May and subsequently held informal consultations. The views expressed by the delegations have been included in the CPC's report on the Programme Plan and can be found in its draft report under symbol E/EC 51/2025/L.4/Addendum 6. While the work of the CPC has already concluded, there is still opportunity for COPUS to provide inputs to the Office as these should be— should the Committee agree— would serve to inform further draft program plans for the Office. Therefore, I would like to invite the Committee to provide inputs to the future programme plans of the Office, with the next one for the year 2027 to be prepared and submitted mid-January 2026. To that end, please allow me to reiterate that the principal focus of the Office's responsibilities continues to be the needs of the Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space and its subsidiary bodies, discharging Secretary-General's responsibilities under the outer space treaties, among which the maintenance of the Register of the Objects Launched in Outer Space, implementing the space applications and UN-sponsored programs, and supporting ICG and SMPH. In line with the Office 2024-2030 strategy and the Space 2030 agenda, the program will further focus on several priorities: supporting COPOS and its working groups to advance inclusive and effective space governance; enhancing Member States' access to space-based solutions for sustainable development, global health, climate action, agriculture, and disaster management. Expanding training, advisory, and legal assistance to help Member States to adopt and implement international legal framework on outer space. Leading the Interagency Meeting on Outer Space Activities to promote coherence and increase collaboration on space-related work among entities of the UN system; scaling up flagship initiatives such as Access to Space for All and the UN Space Bridge and the UN Days for Space Sustainability; supporting Member States in the implementation of the Pact of the Future and preparation of the 4th United Nations Conference on Exploration and Peaceful Uses of Outer Space, UNISPACE-4. To achieve these outcomes, the Office will continue to pursue partnership with agencies, research institutions, industry, and other stakeholders. These collaborations aim to broaden opportunities to access space for science, innovation, education, and capacity building, particularly for developing countries and underrepresented regions. Distinguished delegates, further details regarding the objectives of the Programme Strategy, expected results, and planned deliverables in selected areas of the work of the year 2026 are available in Document A/AT/6, Section VI. In conclusion, allow me to reaffirm the Office's continued dedication to advancing the peaceful exploration of outer space and promoting sustainable development. The Office remains committed to working in close cooperation with all member states to ensure the safe and sustainable use of outer space and to enhance the societal benefits derived from space sciences and technologies. Thank you for your consideration.
